fail_closed_rules: BNG statutory applicability must be evaluated against the application date, development type and current exemptions; a generic BNG rule is not a parcel decision
from 6 August 2026 the 0.2 hectare threshold change is temporal and must not be back-applied to earlier planning applications
the statutory biodiversity metric output is a calculation input, not planning permission or proof of habitat condition without competent survey evidence
a biodiversity gain plan submission is not an approved gain plan and approval is not the underlying planning permission
a registered biodiversity gain site or allocation is not proof that enough units remain available for a target development
off-site biodiversity units, statutory biodiversity credits and on-site gains are distinct mechanisms and must not be collapsed into one availability claim
30-year management and monitoring obligations do not prove future habitat outcomes have already been achieved
irreplaceable habitat impacts are not ordinary metric losses and bespoke compensation is not equivalent to 10 percent BNG
LNRS priority or opportunity mapping is strategic evidence, not planning permission, landowner consent or guaranteed habitat delivery
Priority Habitats Inventory or Habitat Network geometry is inventory or strategic evidence and not a current field survey of a parcel
absence from a national habitat inventory does not prove absence of priority habitat or protected species
SSSI, SAC, SPA, Ramsar, NNR and LNR designations have distinct legal and planning effects and must not be merged
protected-site boundary overlap is not by itself proof of adverse effect, while non-overlap does not exclude indirect effects
HRA screening, appropriate assessment and derogation are separate stages; screening evidence is not approval
protected-species records or modelled risk zones are not proof of current species presence at a target parcel
absence of a species record does not prove species absence; survey need depends on habitat, records, timing and proposal
planning permission and a protected-species licence are separate regimes and one does not automatically supply the other
district-level licensing eligibility or risk zone information for great crested newts is not the licence itself
ancient woodland inventory geometry can be revised and inventory absence does not prove a woodland is non-ancient
possible SAC or potential SPA status must remain distinct from fully designated SAC or SPA status
a metadata record with zero geometry features is NO_DATA for geometry, not evidence that no possible SAC constraint can exist in the future
Planning Data biodiversity-net-gain-assessment currently having zero records is a coverage state, not evidence that no BNG assessment applies
